entries.title: Putnam 2024 A1

entries.input: Let $n$ be a positive integer. Prove that there are positive integers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $2a^{n} + 3b^{n} = 4c^{n}$ if and only if $n \leq 2$.
entries.name: Putnam2024A1Twin
entries.title: Putnam 2024 A1, answer set widened to $n \leq 2$
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2024-a1`: it admits $n = 2$ as well. The quadratic case is the one the 2024 solution rules out first, by reducing $a^{2} + c^{2} \equiv 0 \pmod 3$ on a primitive solution, so a model that agrees here is agreeing with the exact case the problem turns on. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.input: For a positive integer $n$ let $k(n)$ be the number of $1$s in the base-$2$ expansion of $2023n$. Prove that the least value $k$ attains is $3$.
entries.name: Putnam2023B2
entries.conclusion: IsLeast {m : ℕ | ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (Nat.digits 2 (2023 * n)).sum = m} 3
entries.title: Putnam 2023 B2
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: For a positive integer $n$ let $k(n)$ be the number of $1$s in the base-$2$ expansion of $2023n$. Prove that the least value $k$ attains is $2$.
entries.name: Putnam2023B2Twin
entries.conclusion: IsLeast {m : ℕ | ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (Nat.digits 2 (2023 * n)).sum = m} 2
entries.title: Putnam 2023 B2, minimum lowered to two
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2023-b2`: $2$ is not attained, because $2023n = 2^{a} + 2^{b}$ would force $-1$ to be a power of $2$ modulo the factor $7$ of $2023$. Lowering a minimum by one leaves the claim looking exactly as plausible as the true one, which is the point. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

Tightening $\geq$ to $>$ is the smallest possible perturbation of an inequality and cannot be spotted without evaluating the sum. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.title: Putnam 2018 A1

entries.input: Let $A$ be the set of integers $n$ with $1 \leq n \leq 2021$ and $\gcd(n, 2021) = 1$, and for a nonnegative integer $j$ put $S(j) = \sum_{n \in A} n^{j}$. Prove that $2021$ divides $S(j)$ exactly when $j$ is a multiple of neither $42$ nor $46$.
entries.name: Putnam2021A5
entries.conclusion: (2021 ∣ ∑ n ∈ (Finset.Icc 1 2021).filter (fun n => Nat.gcd n 2021 = 1), n ^ j) ↔ ¬ (42 ∣ j) ∧ ¬ (46 ∣ j)
entries.title: Putnam 2021 A5

entries.input: Determine which integers have the form $A^{3} + B^{3} + C^{3} - 3ABC$ with $A$, $B$, $C$ nonnegative integers. Prove that an integer $n$ has this form exactly when $n \geq 0$ and $n$ is congruent to neither $3$ nor $6$ modulo $9$.
entries.name: Putnam2019A1
entries.title: Putnam 2019 A1

entries.input: Determine which integers have the form $A^{3} + B^{3} + C^{3} - 3ABC$ with $A$, $B$, $C$ nonnegative integers. Prove that an integer $n$ has this form exactly when $n \geq 0$.
entries.name: Putnam2019A1Twin
entries.title: Putnam 2019 A1, congruence condition dropped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2019-a1`: dropping the modulus condition claims every nonnegative integer is represented, and $3$ is not. Nonnegativity is the half of the answer that is easy to see, so a model reading only that far agrees; the residues $3$ and $6$ modulo $9$ are the half that has to be proved. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.

entries.input: Let $m_0$ and $n_0$ be distinct positive integers, and for each $k \geq 1$ let $m_k$ and $n_k$ be the coprime positive integers with $m_k / n_k = (2m_{k-1} + 1)/(2n_{k-1} + 1)$. Prove that $2m_k + 1$ and $2n_k + 1$ are coprime for all but finitely many $k$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A1
entries.binders: (m n : ℕ → ℕ) (hpos : ∀ k, 0 < m k ∧ 0 < n k) (hne : m 0 ≠ n 0) (hcop : ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → Nat.Coprime (m k) (n k)) (hrec : ∀ k, m (k + 1) * (2 * n k + 1) = n (k + 1) * (2 * m k + 1))
entries.conclusion: {k : ℕ | ¬ Nat.Coprime (2 * m k + 1) (2 * n k + 1)}.Finite
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A1
entries.witness_note: The binders constrain two sequences by a mutual recursion together with coprimality at every index, so closing them under `∃` needs the recursively defined pair and a proof at every index. Recorded as a debt rather than guessed.

entries.input: Let $b_0 = 0$ and $b_{n+1} = 2b_n^{2} + b_n + 1$ for $n \geq 0$. Prove that for every $k \geq 1$ the number $b_{2^{k+1}} - 2b_{2^{k}}$ is divisible by $2^{2k+2}$ but not by $2^{2k+3}$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A6
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A6
entries.witness: ⟨fun n => Nat.rec (motive := fun _ => ℤ) 0 (fun _ x => 2 * x ^ 2 + x + 1) n, rfl, fun _ => rfl, 1, le_refl 1, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $b_0 = 0$ and $b_{n+1} = 2b_n^{2} + b_n + 1$ for $n \geq 0$. Prove that for every $k \geq 1$ the number $b_{2^{k+1}} - 2b_{2^{k}}$ is divisible by $2^{2k+3}$.
entries.name: Putnam2025A6Twin
entries.title: Putnam 2025 A6, exponent raised by one
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2025-a6`: the true statement is that the $2$-adic valuation is *exactly* $2k+2$, so raising the exponent by one turns a sharp result into a false one. At $k = 1$ the difference is $2768 = 2^4 \cdot 173$. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
entries.witness: ⟨fun n => Nat.rec (motive := fun _ => ℤ) 0 (fun _ x => 2 * x ^ 2 + x + 1) n, rfl, fun _ => rfl, 1, le_refl 1, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $S$ be a nonempty set of positive integers such that whenever $n \in S$, every positive divisor of $2025^{n} - 15^{n}$ also lies in $S$. Prove that $S$ contains every positive integer.
entries.name: Putnam2025B3
entries.binders: (S : Set ℕ) (hne : S.Nonempty) (hpos : ∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) (hdiv : ∀ n ∈ S, ∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → d ∣ (2025 ^ n - 15 ^ n) → d ∈ S)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 B3
entries.witness: ⟨{n : ℕ | 0 < n}, ⟨1, Nat.one_pos⟩, fun n hn => hn, fun n _ d hd _ => hd, trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $S$ be a set of positive integers such that whenever $n \in S$, every positive divisor of $2025^{n} - 15^{n}$ also lies in $S$. Prove that $S$ contains every positive integer.
entries.name: Putnam2025B3Twin
entries.binders: (S : Set ℕ) (hpos : ∀ n ∈ S, 0 < n) (hdiv : ∀ n ∈ S, ∀ d : ℕ, 0 < d → d ∣ (2025 ^ n - 15 ^ n) → d ∈ S)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 B3, the nonemptiness hypothesis dropped
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2025-b3`: without `S.Nonempty` the empty set satisfies both remaining hypotheses vacuously and contains no positive integer at all. Nonemptiness is what starts the induction -- it is how $1$ gets into $S$ -- so the twin removes the one premise the proof cannot do without. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
entries.witness: ⟨(∅ : Set ℕ), fun n hn => absurd hn (Set.notMem_empty n), fun n hn => absurd hn (Set.notMem_empty n), trivial⟩

entries.input: Let $p > 3$ be prime and, for $k \in \{1, \dots, p-1\}$, let $I(k)$ be the element of $\{1, \dots, p-1\}$ with $k \cdot I(k) \equiv 1 \pmod p$. Prove that the number of $k \in \{1, \dots, p-2\}$ with $I(k+1) < I(k)$ is greater than $p/4 - 1$.
entries.name: Putnam2025B5
entries.binders: (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) (h3 : 3 < p) (I : ℕ → ℕ) (hI : ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ p - 1 → 1 ≤ I k ∧ I k ≤ p - 1 ∧ k * I k ≡ 1 [MOD p])
entries.title: Putnam 2025 B5
entries.witness: ⟨5, by norm_num, by norm_num, fun k => if k = 1 then 1 else if k = 2 then 3 else if k = 3 then 2 else 4, by intro k h1 h2; interval_cases k <;> simp [Nat.ModEq], trivial⟩

entries.input: Prove that $1/4$ is the largest real number $r$ for which there is a function $g$ from the positive integers to the positive integers with $g(n+1) - g(n) \geq (g(g(n)))^{r}$ for every positive integer $n$.
entries.name: Putnam2025B6
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {r : ℝ | ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < n → 0 < g n) ∧ ∀ n, 0 < n → ((g (g n) : ℝ)) ^ r ≤ (g (n + 1) : ℝ) - (g n : ℝ)} (1 / 4)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 B6
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: Prove that $1/2$ is the largest real number $r$ for which there is a function $g$ from the positive integers to the positive integers with $g(n+1) - g(n) \geq (g(g(n)))^{r}$ for every positive integer $n$.
entries.name: Putnam2025B6Twin
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {r : ℝ | ∃ g : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < n → 0 < g n) ∧ ∀ n, 0 < n → ((g (g n) : ℝ)) ^ r ≤ (g (n + 1) : ℝ) - (g n : ℝ)} (1 / 2)
entries.title: Putnam 2025 B6, constant raised to one half
entries.rationale: A soundness twin for `putnam-2025-b6`: no such $g$ exists for any $r > 1/4$, so $1/2$ is not even in the set, let alone its greatest element. $1/2$ is the constant a reader guesses from $g(n) = n^{2}$ without checking which exponent that choice actually supports, which is $1/4$. It states nothing the paper asked, so it cites no occurrence.
entries.witness_note: The entry has no binders: it states one closed claim about a single set, so there is nothing for A6 to existentially close and a `trivial` witness would record coverage that was never obtained.

entries.input: Determine the positive integers $N$ for which the sphere $x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = N$ has an inscribed regular tetrahedron with integer coordinates. Prove that these are exactly the $N$ of the form $3m^{2}$ with $m$ a positive integer.
entries.name: Putnam2021A3
entries.conclusion: (∃ v : Fin 4 → (Fin 3 → ℤ), Function.Injective v ∧ (∀ i, ∑ t, v i t ^ 2 = (N : ℤ)) ∧ ∀ i j k l : Fin 4, i ≠ j → k ≠ l → ∑ t, (v i t - v j t) ^ 2 = ∑ t, (v k t - v l t) ^ 2) ↔ ∃ m : ℕ, 0 < m ∧ N = 3 * m ^ 2
entries.title: Putnam 2021 A3

entries.input: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $q(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{p-1} a_k x^k$ in $\mathbb{F}_p[x]$, where $a_k$ is $k^{(p-1)/2}$ reduced modulo $p$. Prove that $(p-1)/2$ is the greatest $n$ for which $(x-1)^{n}$ divides $q(x)$.
entries.name: Putnam2019A5
entries.conclusion: IsGreatest {n : ℕ | (Polynomial.X - 1) ^ n ∣ (∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 (p - 1), Polynomial.C ((k : ZMod p) ^ ((p - 1) / 2)) * Polynomial.X ^ k)} ((p - 1) / 2)
entries.title: Putnam 2019 A5
